answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks via hardware remote attestation. Agents run in secure enclaves, yielding cryptographic quotes signed by vendor silicon. An adversary incurs the verifiable hardware cost of procuring physical chips across a server orchard. Networks enforce a marble baseline of enclave uniqueness, attaching saffron penalties to clustered keys. However, this depends on trusted chipmakers and remains susceptible to side-channel exploits.
